But the Board has no Chairperson and no Members to decide anything. Six months before most duties begin, here's where India's privacy law stands. Consent managers WHAT THEY ARE One dashboard for your consents A registered platform through which you give, manage, review and withdraw consent across many businesses. It acts on your behalf, not the business's. 1 An Indian company with a net worth of at least ₹2 crore. 2 An independently certified platform, against standards the Board publishes. 3 Fair, conflict-free management, with duties written into its articles. Most businesses are data fiduciaries, not consent managers, and don't register. And for now, there's no one to approve applications. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 04 / 08

A law without a regulator is a law on hold 1 No approvals. Consent managers can apply, but no one can register them. 2 No standards. The Board is meant to publish certification standards and guidance. None yet. 3 No time to build capacity. From May 2027, it must handle complaints and inquiries, including from cases sent by courts. 4 Appoint now, and transparently. Name independent members, publish the process, and staff the Board well before May. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 06 / 08

FOR BUSINESSES · SIX MONTHS TO GO Don't wait for the Board NOW TO FEBRUARY MARCH TO MAY Know your data Build the controls Map what personal data you Consent that's as easy to hold, where and why withdraw as to give Flag children's data and any Encryption, access controls, SDF risk logs kept one year Add data-processing clauses A breach playbook with a 72- to vendor contracts hour report Draft clear, itemised notices A grievance contact and erasure schedule The duties apply from May 2027 whether or not the regulator is ready. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 07 / 08

TA K E AWAY The law's clock is running, even if the regulator isn't. One year in, India has privacy rules but no one to enforce them. The government needs to appoint the Board now. Businesses need to use the next six months, not wait for it. Adv.
